question.text: 'Nilgiri Mid-Market AIF' has two named key persons: Ms. Radhika Swamy and Mr. Vikram Bhatnagar. The side letter with a pension fund LP contains a 'key-person event' clause. What is the TYPICAL operative consequence of a key-person event under such clauses?

answer.text: Immediate termination of the IMA without any LP vote

Prohibition on new investments while key persons are unavailable, with investors entitled to compulsory redemption/exit without charges unless a suitable replacement is found within the pre-agreed timelines and SEBI is informed
The manager must personally compensate each LP for notional losses

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, a key-person clause prohibits new investments by the fund when the named key persons are unavailable. Investors typically ask for the right to compulsory redemption or exit without charges unless a suitable replacement is found within the pre-agreed timelines and the same is informed to SEBI. The Trap: Immediate termination of the IMA without any LP vote is too draconian and is not the typical operative consequence. An automatic 50% fee waiver is not part of the standard key-person mechanic. Personal compensation by the manager for notional LP losses is not contemplated by the workbook description. Note: Two limbs travel together — a prohibition on new investments during key-person unavailability, and the investor's right to compulsory redemption/exit without charges if a replacement is not found within the agreed window (with SEBI informed).
